figs.name: rtd-sensor-connections-4-wire-diagram
figs.alt: rtd sensor connections 4 wire diagram with current leads L1 L4 and sense leads L2 L3
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing a 4 wire RTD: current Is flows through L1 and L4 while L2 and L3 sense the voltage E0 across the RTD only.
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 490" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>4 wire RTD connection with separate current and sensing leads</title>
<rect width="800" height="490" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">4 Wire RTD: Separate Current and Sense Leads</text>
<rect x="560" y="70" width="220" height="340" rx="14" fill="#eef2ff" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="670" y="98" font-size="19" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Transmitter</text>
<polyline points="150,200 136,208.33333333333334 164,225.0 136,241.66666666666669 164,258.3333333333333 136,275.0 164,291.6666666666667 150,300" fill="none" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="3.5"/>
<text x="118" y="245" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="end">RTD</text>
<text x="118" y="269" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="end">RT</text>
<polyline points="150,200 150,120 720,120 720,222" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3.5"/>
<rect x="330" y="110" width="50" height="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="355" y="102" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">L1, red</text>
<circle cx="560" cy="120" r="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<polyline points="150,200 620,200 620,222" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3.5"/>
<rect x="330" y="190" width="50" height="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="355" y="182" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">L2, red</text>
<circle cx="560" cy="200" r="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<polyline points="150,300 620,300 620,278" fill="none" stroke="#9ca3af" stroke-width="3.5"/>
<rect x="330" y="290" width="50" height="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="355" y="282" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">L3, white</text>
<circle cx="560" cy="300" r="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<polyline points="150,300 150,380 720,380 720,278" fill="none" stroke="#9ca3af" stroke-width="3.5"/>
<rect x="330" y="370" width="50" height="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="355" y="362" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">L4, white</text>
<circle cx="560" cy="380" r="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<circle cx="150" cy="200" r="5" fill="#1a2b4a"/>
<circle cx="150" cy="300" r="5" fill="#1a2b4a"/>
<line x1="270" y1="120" x2="230" y2="120" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<line x1="230" y1="380" x2="270" y2="380" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<circle cx="620" cy="250" r="28" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="620" y="257" font-size="20" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">V</text>
<circle cx="720" cy="250" r="28" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<line x1="720" y1="268" x2="720" y2="234" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="670" y="257" font-size="18" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Is</text>

<text x="400" y="440" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">E0 = Is × RT: lead and contact resistances drop out</text>

figs.name: rtd-sensor-connections-3-wire-cable-flowchart
figs.alt: flowchart for connecting a 3 wire RTD with a 4 wire cable to a transmitter
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing the two correct ways to wire a 3 wire RTD with a 4 wire cable: 4 wire mode with all wires, or 3 wire mode with one unused.
figs.after_h2: Solutions for a 3-wire RTD and a 4-wire cable
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 560" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Flowchart for wiring a 3 wire RTD with a 4 wire cable</title>
<rect width="800" height="560" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">3 Wire RTD with a 4 Wire Cable: What to Do</text>
<rect x="220" y="60" width="360" height="56" rx="10" fill="#eef2ff" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="400.0" y="82.3" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">3 wire RTD, but only</text>
<text x="400.0" y="106.3" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">a 4 wire cable on hand</text>
<line x1="400" y1="116" x2="400" y2="133" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<polygon points="400,135.0 570.0,185 400,235.0 230.0,185" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="400" y="180.3" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Can the transmitter</text>
<text x="400" y="202.3" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">run 4 wire mode?</text>
<polyline points="230,185 145,185 145,248" fill="none" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="188" y="175" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Yes</text>
<polyline points="570,185 655,185 655,248" fill="none" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="612" y="175" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">No</text>
<rect x="20" y="250" width="250" height="90" rx="10" fill="#eef2ff" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="145.0" y="277.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Solution 1</text>
<text x="145.0" y="300.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">set 4 wire mode,</text>
<text x="145.0" y="323.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">use all four wires</text>
<rect x="530" y="250" width="250" height="90" rx="10" fill="#eef2ff" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="655.0" y="277.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Solution 2</text>
<text x="655.0" y="300.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">keep 3 wire mode,</text>
<text x="655.0" y="323.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">leave 4th wire unused</text>
<polyline points="145,340 145,420 198,420" fill="none" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<polyline points="655,340 655,420 602,420" fill="none" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<rect x="200" y="390" width="400" height="60" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="400.0" y="414.3" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Sensing wires run</text>
<text x="400.0" y="438.3" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">directly to the RTD</text>
<line x1="400" y1="450" x2="400" y2="478" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<rect x="110" y="480" width="580" height="64" rx="10" fill="#fef2f2" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="400.0" y="506.3" font-size="18" fill="#991b1b" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Never parallel current carrying wires</text>
<text x="400.0" y="530.3" font-size="18" fill="#991b1b" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">or jumper sensing terminals</text>
</svg>

figs.name: rtd-sensor-connections-2-3-4-wire-comparison-infographic
figs.alt: comparison of 2 wire, 3 wire and 4 wire RTD connections with accuracy and wire colours
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog comparing 2, 3 and 4 wire RTD connections by what they measure, accuracy, IEC 60751 wire colours and typical use.
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 550" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Comparison of 2 wire, 3 wire and 4 wire RTD connections</title>
<rect width="800" height="550" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2, 3 and 4 Wire RTD Connections Compared</text>
<rect x="20" y="55" width="240" height="430" rx="14" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="140" y="88" font-size="22" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2 Wire</text>
<polyline points="80,110 69,115.83333333333333 91,127.5 69,139.16666666666666 91,150.83333333333331 69,162.5 91,174.16666666666666 80,180" fill="none" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="3"/>

<text x="140" y="222" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Measures</text>
<text x="140" y="246" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">RT + L1 + L2</text>
<text x="140" y="288" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Accuracy</text>
<text x="140" y="312" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Lowest</text>
<text x="140" y="354" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Colours IEC 60751</text>

<text x="140" y="444" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Short runs, low cost</text>
<rect x="280" y="55" width="240" height="430" rx="14" fill="#eef2ff" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="400" y="88" font-size="22" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">3 Wire</text>

<line x1="340" y1="110" x2="495" y2="110" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3.5"/>
<line x1="340" y1="180" x2="495" y2="180" stroke="#9ca3af" stroke-width="3.5"/>
<polyline points="375,110 375,132 495,132" fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3.5"/>
<circle cx="375" cy="110" r="5" fill="#1a2b4a"/>
<text x="400" y="222" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Measures</text>
<text x="400" y="246" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Leads cancel if equal</text>
<text x="400" y="288" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Accuracy</text>
<text x="400" y="312" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Good</text>
<text x="400" y="354" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Colours IEC 60751</text>
<text x="400" y="378" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Red, Red, White</text>
<text x="400" y="420" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Best for</text>
<text x="400" y="444" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Industrial processes</text>
<rect x="540" y="55" width="240" height="430" rx="14" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="660" y="88" font-size="22" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">4 Wire</text>
<polyline points="600,110 589,115.83333333333333 611,127.5 589,139.16666666666666 611,150.83333333333331 589,162.5 611,174.16666666666666 600,180" fill="none" stroke="#4338ca" stroke-width="3"/>
<line x1="600" y1="110" x2="755" y2="110" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3.5"/>

<circle cx="635" cy="180" r="5" fill="#1a2b4a"/>
<text x="660" y="222" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Measures</text>
<text x="660" y="246" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">RT only, E0 = Is × RT</text>
<text x="660" y="288" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Accuracy</text>
<text x="660" y="312" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Highest</text>
<text x="660" y="354" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Colours IEC 60751</text>
<text x="660" y="378" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Red, Red, White, White</text>
<text x="660" y="420" font-size="17" fill="#312e81" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Best for</text>
<text x="660" y="444" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Laboratory accuracy</text>
<text x="400" y="522" font-size="18" fill="#991b1b" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Never jumper sensing terminals: it turns any setup into 2 wire</text>
